title: The Festival That Changed Its Questions
fact_notes: 人物・制度・具体的な出来事は架空の教材例・思考実験。実在の調査・統計・実証結果を示すものではない。制作台帳は来歴確認用。

sentences.en: At an imaginary international youth festival, each school was invited to prepare an exhibition about life in its country.
sentences.ja: 架空の国際青少年交流祭で各校は自国の生活について展示するよう招かれた。

sentences.en: Many groups selected familiar symbols such as traditional clothing, famous buildings, and popular dishes.
sentences.ja: 多くのグループは伝統衣装、有名な建物、人気料理など身近な象徴を選んだ。

sentences.en: The organizers expected these displays to encourage lively conversations among visitors from different backgrounds.
sentences.ja: 主催者は展示が異なる背景の来場者間の活発な会話を促すと期待した。

sentences.en: However, one student noticed that most visitors simply took photographs before moving to the next display.
sentences.ja: しかしある生徒は多くの来場者が写真を撮るだけで次の展示へ移ると気づいた。

sentences.en: She suggested replacing some of the descriptive labels with questions about ordinary choices and experiences.
sentences.ja: 説明用ラベルの一部を日常の選択や経験についての質問に置き換えることを提案した。

sentences.en: For instance, a display of school lunches could invite visitors to describe how meals were organized at their own schools.
sentences.ja: 例えば学校給食の展示は来場者に自校の食事の仕組みを説明するよう促せる。

sentences.en: Instead of presenting a single routine as representative of an entire nation, the students could explain where their examples came from.
sentences.ja: 単一の日課を国全体の代表として紹介せず、例の出所を説明できる。

sentences.en: They could also ask visitors whether their experiences differed from those presented in the exhibition.
sentences.ja: 来場者の経験が展示されたものと異なるか尋ねることもできる。

sentences.en: The organizers decided to test the suggestion at a small portion of the festival before changing every display.
sentences.ja: 主催者は全展示を変更する前に祭の一部で提案を試すことにした。

sentences.en: Each participating group collected short responses from visitors who volunteered to share their experiences.
sentences.ja: 参加グループは自ら経験を共有する来場者から短い回答を集めた。

sentences.en: Several conversations revealed differences within countries that had originally been presented as relatively uniform communities.
sentences.ja: いくつかの会話で当初比較的均一な共同体として紹介された国の内部の違いが明らかになった。

sentences.en: The students discovered that a visitor from the same country might describe a completely different everyday routine.
sentences.ja: 同じ国の来場者でも全く異なる日課を説明する場合があると分かった。

sentences.en: The festival staff encouraged participants to distinguish observations from broad conclusions about national characteristics.
sentences.ja: 祭の職員は観察と国民的特徴についての広い結論を区別するよう参加者に促した。

sentences.en: They also reminded the students that a few voluntary responses could not establish how common a particular practice was.
sentences.ja: 少数の自発的回答では特定の慣行がどのくらい一般的か確定できないことも注意した。

sentences.en: Nevertheless, the responses were useful for identifying topics that deserved further discussion and more careful investigation.
sentences.ja: それでも回答はさらなる議論や慎重な調査に値する話題の特定に役立った。

sentences.en: The final exhibition included several contrasting experiences without ranking them according to their supposed cultural importance.
sentences.ja: 最終展示では文化的重要性を推測して順位づけせず対照的な経験をいくつか含めた。

sentences.en: The project illustrates that international understanding involves more than acquiring a collection of memorable facts about other countries.
sentences.ja: この活動は国際理解が他国についての印象的事実を集める以上のことを含むと示す。

sentences.en: It also requires recognizing the limits of one's examples and allowing other people to describe their own experiences.
sentences.ja: 自分の例の限界を認め、他者が自分の経験を語れるようにすることも必要だ。

sentences.en: A well-designed cultural exchange can make unfamiliar experiences accessible without turning individual stories into unsupported generalizations.
sentences.ja: よく設計された文化交流は個人の話を根拠のない一般化にせず未知の経験を理解しやすくできる。

sentences.en: For these students, the festival became an opportunity to ask better questions rather than simply provide more impressive answers.
sentences.ja: 生徒たちにとって祭は印象的な答えを増やすだけでなく、よりよい問いを立てる機会になった。

vocabulary.definition: using one thing in place of another
a regular way of doing things
statements applied to a whole group

questions.prompt: What did the schools initially display?

options: Visitors often took photos and moved on.
questions.explanation_ja: 写真を撮って移動した。
日常経験についての問い。

questions.prompt: Why explain where examples came from?
options: To avoid presenting one experience as typical of everyone.
To prevent cultural differences from being discussed.
To prove all schools are identical.
questions.explanation_ja: 一例を国全体と扱わない。

options: Each country has one fixed routine.
Experiences can differ within the same country.

questions.prompt: What did staff caution about the responses?
options: They could not establish how widespread a practice was.
They could prove national trends exactly.
They had to be discarded entirely.
They were mandatory for every visitor.
questions.explanation_ja: 少数回答では普及度を確定できない。

options: To show variety without assuming a hierarchy.
Broad claims about a larger group.
One visitor represents an entire country.
Cultural exchange benefits from dialogue and awareness of the limits of examples.
questions.explanation_ja: 対話と例の限界を重視。

grammar.focus: before moving to the next display
as representative of an entire nation

grammar.explanation_ja: 過去完了受動態で以前の紹介を示す。

grammar.focus: without turning individual stories into unsupported generalizations
